title: The Minimum Subset Vertex Cover Problem for the Optimal Placement of E3 HEMP Arrestors
content: This paper demonstrates that a power grid may be fully protected from E3 high-altitude magnetic pulses (HEMP) using E3 arrestor devices placed at substations that represent any vertex cover of the grid. This serves as a simple linear time check to see if pre-existing E3 arrestor-type assets are sufficient for the mitigation of E3 HEMP waveforms. The algorithm to determine where to place new arrestor devices is computationally inexpensive, with a runtime of 8 ms for an 18-bus test case and a runtime of 486 ms for a 150-bus test case in MATLAB to determine the bounding case approximation. The algorithm accomplishes this by finding the minimum vertex cover of the grid and placing E3 arrestor devices in those locations. Since computing the minimum vertex cover is NP-Hard, the algorithm approximates this by computing the solution of a linear program combined with a heuristic based on the four color theorem and knowledge of the permissible substations to upgrade (i.e. substations with E3 arrestors). If the solution exists, it guarantees the near zeroing out of flux across all transformers. If some flux can be tolerated, there may exist an even smaller set of substations to protect that allow system specifications to be met. Additionally, if there already exist devices that make up a vertex cover on the grid, then it is guaranteed that the grid is already protected from E3 disturbances. The check for this distribution of devices is linear in time. The vertex cover solution may be used with other optimization techniques as a homotopy to find the minimum number of required E3 arrestors. The minimum vertex cover is the bounding case solution for the E3 arrestor device.
